title: Tony Casillas and His 1985 Lombardi Award at Oklahoma
question: Did Tony Casillas win the Lombardi Award at Oklahoma?
answer: Yes. Nose guard Tony Casillas won the Lombardi Award in 1985, becoming the second Sooner to win it, and helped lead Oklahoma to the national championship that season. He was a consensus All-American in 1984 and 1985.
summary: Tony Casillas won the 1985 Lombardi Award as OU's nose guard, the second Sooner to win it, then went No. 2 overall in the NFL draft and won two Super Bowls.
body: Barry Switzer coached a lot of great defenders, and he singled out Tony Casillas as perhaps the greatest defensive lineman ever to play at Oklahoma. The nose guard from Tulsa backed that up in 1985 by winning the Lombardi Award, given to the top lineman or linebacker in college football. He was only the second Sooner to win it.

Casillas lined up for OU from 1982 to 1985 and was a consensus All-American in both 1984 and 1985. He was named Big Eight Defensive Player of the Year and was chosen as a national lineman of the year by UPI. He finished his career with 213 tackles and 18 sacks, numbers that came from a player offenses could never quite scheme away from.

His senior season ended in the best way possible. Casillas was a central piece of the 1985 defense that carried Oklahoma to the national title, the program's first in a decade. He was later voted the Big Eight's Defensive Player of the Decade for the 1980s, and the National Football Foundation recognizes him as the College Defensive Player of the Decade.

Casillas was also a strong student who earned a public relations degree and academic all-conference honors. The Atlanta Falcons drafted him second overall in 1986, and he went on to win two Super Bowls with the Dallas Cowboys during a long NFL career.
The College Football Hall of Fame inducted Casillas in 2004, a fitting honor for one of the most disruptive interior defenders the Sooners have produced.
